sentences: In a Prohibition-era city, the hero is a jazz saxophone player and an irresponsible, impulsive gambler and ladies' man; his anxious friend is a jazz double bass player.
They work in a speakeasy owned by a local mob boss.
Tipped off by an informant, the police raid the joint.
The hero and his friend escape but accidentally witness the mob boss and his henchmen gunning down the informant and his gang in revenge (an incident inspired by a real massacre).
The mob boss and his gang see them as they flee.

Broke, terrified, and desperate to leave the city, the hero and his friend disguise themselves as women so they can join a bandleader and her group, an all-female band headed to another city by train.
On the train, they befriend the singer, the band's vocalist and ukulele player.
The hero and his friend become obsessed with the singer and compete for her affections while maintaining their disguises.
The singer confides to the hero that she has sworn off (male) saxophone players, who have taken advantage of her in the past.
She hopes to find a gentle, bespectacled millionaire at their destination.
The hero and his friend become close friends with the singer during a late-night party on the train, while struggling to remember that flirting with her would compromise their cover.
After arriving in the other city, the hero woos the singer by posing as the heir to an oil company's fortune, affecting a movie star's accent while feigning indifference to her.
An aging, multi-divorced suitor—an actual millionaire—persistently pursues the disguised friend, whose refusals only fuel his desire.
After the suitor invites the friend to dinner on his yacht, the hero convinces his friend to keep the suitor occupied onshore, so the hero can pass the yacht off as his own and entertain the singer.
As the heir, he tells the singer that psychological trauma from the death of a former lover has left him impotent, but he would immediately marry anyone who could cure him.
The singer tries to arouse him, with considerable success.
Meanwhile, the friend and the suitor tango until dawn.
Back at the hotel, the friend announces that he has accepted the suitor's proposal of marriage, anticipating a divorce and cash settlement when the ruse is revealed.
The hero convinces his friend that he cannot marry the suitor.

The hotel hosts a conference for an opera society, a front for a national mob meeting, presided over by the syndicate chief—who already has a grudge against the mob boss over the murder of the informant.
The mob boss and his men arrive, and this time see through the hero and his friend's disguises.
Fearing for their lives, the hero and his friend realize they must quit the band and leave the hotel.
The hero breaks up with the singer over the telephone, telling her that he must marry a woman of his father's choosing and move to another country, leaving her heartbroken.
In male disguises, the hero and his friend evade the mob boss's men by hiding under a table at the syndicate banquet, where the syndicate chief has the mob boss and his gang gunned down.
The hero and his friend are spotted as they flee through the hotel.
They revert to women's clothing to evade capture.
On the way out, the hero, dressed as a woman, sees the singer onstage singing a lament to lost love, kisses her, then rejoins his friend in their flight.
Realizing that her bandmate and the heir are the same person, the singer follows them.
Still dressed as a woman, the friend persuades the suitor to take him and the hero away on his yacht.
The singer unexpectedly joins them on the suitor's launch just as it leaves the dock.
Removing his disguise, the hero confesses to the singer and tells her that she deserves better, but the singer wants him anyway, realizing he is the first man to genuinely care for her.

Meanwhile, the friend, in disguise, tries to get out of his engagement, listing reasons why "she" and the suitor cannot marry—she can't wear his mother's wedding gown because she's "not built the same", is not a natural blonde, smokes, cannot have children, has been living with a saxophone player—none of which bother the suitor.
Exasperated, the friend rips off his wig and says, "I'm a man!" in his normal voice.
Still unperturbed and smiling, the suitor replies "Well, nobody's perfect!" leaving the friend speechless.
In 1938 in the city, at the end of the country's regime, the heroine is a free-spirited young woman studying to become a nun at the abbey.
However, her youthful enthusiasm and lack of discipline cause some concern.
The abbess sends the heroine to the villa of the retired naval officer, the captain, to be the new governess to his seven children.
The captain has been raising his children using strict military discipline following their mother's death, however they have scared away several governesses by playing tricks.
Although the children misbehave at first, the heroine responds with kindness and patience, and soon the children come to trust and respect her.
While the captain is away in another city, the heroine makes play clothes for the children out of drapes that are to be changed.
She takes them around the city and the mountains while teaching them how to sing.

When the captain returns to the villa with the baroness, a wealthy socialite, and their mutual friend, they are greeted by the heroine and the children returning from a boat ride on the lake, which ends abruptly when their boat overturns.
Displeased by his children's clothes and activities along with the heroine's impassioned appeal that he get closer to his children, the captain attempts to fire the heroine.
However, he hears singing from inside the house and is astonished to see his children singing for the baroness.
Filled with emotion, the captain joins his children, singing for the first time in years.
The captain apologizes to the heroine and asks her to stay.
Impressed by the children's singing, the friend proposes that he enter them in the upcoming festival, but the captain disapproves of letting his children sing in public.
During a grand party at the villa, where guests in formal attire waltz in the ballroom, the heroine and the children look on from the garden terrace.
When the captain notices the heroine teaching one of the children the traditional Ländler folk dance, he steps in and partners the heroine in a graceful performance, culminating in a close embrace.
Confused about her feelings, the heroine blushes and breaks away.
Later, the baroness, who noticed the captain's attraction to the heroine, hides her jealousy by indirectly convincing the heroine that she must return to the abbey.
The abbess learns that the heroine has stayed in seclusion to avoid her growing romantic feelings for the captain, so she encourages her to return to the villa to look for her purpose in life.
When the heroine returns to the villa, she learns about the captain's engagement to the baroness and agrees to stay until they find a replacement governess.

However, the baroness learns that the captain's feelings for the heroine have not changed, so she peacefully calls off the engagement and returns to the other city while encouraging the captain to express his feelings for the heroine.
After which, the two get married.
While the couple is on their honeymoon, the friend enters the children into the festival against their father's wishes.

Having learned that the country has been annexed by a foreign regime, the couple return to their home, where the captain receives a telegram, ordering him to report to a naval base to accept a commission in the regime's navy.
Strongly opposed to the regime and its ideology, the captain tells his family they must leave the country immediately.
That night, the family attempt to flee to another country, but they are stopped by a group of militiamen, led by the regional leader, waiting outside the villa.
To cover his family's tracks, the captain maintains they are headed to the festival to perform.
The regional leader insists on escorting them to the festival, after which his men will accompany the captain to the naval base.
Later that night at the festival, after their final number, the family slips away while the friend stalls for them.
The family seeks shelter at the abbey, where the abbess hides them in the cemetery crypt.
The regional leader and his men soon arrive and search the abbey, but the family is able to escape using the caretaker's car.
When the regional leader's men attempt to pursue, they discover their cars will not start since two of the nuns have sabotaged their engines.
The next morning—after driving to the border—the family walks on foot across the frontier into the other country to safety and freedom.
In the city, the real estate secretary embezzles $40,000 in cash from her employer after hearing her boyfriend complain that his debts are delaying their marriage.
She sets off to drive to the boyfriend's home in the town, switching cars in another town after an encounter with a suspicious policeman.
A rainstorm forces the secretary to stop at the secluded motel a few miles from the town.
The proprietor, whose house overlooks the motel, registers the secretary (who uses an alias) and invites her to dinner with him in the motel's office.
When the proprietor returns to his house to retrieve the food, the secretary overhears him arguing with his mother about his desire to dine with the secretary.
After returning, he discusses his hobby as a taxidermist, his mother's "illness", and how everyone is in a "private trap" they cannot escape.
When the secretary suggests that the proprietor should have his mother institutionalized, he becomes agitated and insists that she is harmless.
The secretary decides to drive back to the city in the morning to return the stolen money.
As she showers, a shadowy figure enters the bathroom with a kitchen knife and stabs her to death.
Moments later, the proprietor runs to the motel to find the secretary dead.
He hurriedly cleans up the murder scene and places the secretary's body, her belongings, and, unbeknownst to him, the hidden cash in her car before sinking the vehicle in a swamp.
The secretary's sister arrives in the town a week later, tells the boyfriend about the theft, and demands information about the secretary's whereabouts.
He denies knowing anything about the secretary's disappearance.
A private investigator approaches them, stating that he has been hired to retrieve the money.
He stops at the motel and questions the proprietor, whose nervousness and inconsistent answers arouse his suspicion.
The investigator examines the guest register and discovers from some handwriting in it that the secretary spent a night in the motel.
When the investigator infers from his conversation with the proprietor that the secretary had spoken to his mother, the investigator asks to speak to her, but the proprietor refuses.
The investigator leaves and calls the sister to tell her of his suspicions.
When he returns and enters the house to search for the proprietor's mother, a shadowy figure at the top of the stairs stabs him to death.
When the boyfriend and the sister do not hear back from the investigator, the boyfriend goes to the motel to look for him.
The boyfriend spots a silhouette in a second-floor window of the house and assumes it is the proprietor's mother, who is unresponsive to the boyfriend's calls.
The sister and the boyfriend alert the local sheriff, who tells them the proprietor's mother killed herself and her lover with strychnine poisoning 10 years earlier.
The sheriff suggests that the investigator lied to the boyfriend and the sister so he could pursue the secretary and the money.
Convinced that something happened to the investigator, the sister and the boyfriend drive to the motel and check in.
The boyfriend distracts the proprietor in the office while the sister sneaks into the house.
Suspicious, the proprietor knocks the boyfriend out.
As the proprietor heads to the house, the sister hides in the fruit cellar and discovers the mummified body of the proprietor's mother.
The sister screams in horror, and the proprietor, wearing a dress and a wig, enters the cellar and attacks her with a knife, only to be subdued by a recovered boyfriend.
At the police station, a psychiatrist explains to the sister, the boyfriend, and the sheriff that the proprietor murdered his domineering mother and her lover out of jealousy.

Unable to bear the guilt, he stole his mother's corpse and treated it as if she were still alive, then re-created his mother as an alternate personality, as jealous and possessive toward the proprietor as she had been in life.
Whenever the proprietor was attracted to a woman, "Mother" would take over; under the "Mother" personality, the proprietor killed two women before he killed the secretary and the investigator.
The psychiatrist concludes that "Mother" has now completely submerged the proprietor's personality.
The proprietor sits in a jail cell and hears his mother's voice stating the murders were his doing and that she would never be suspected.
The secretary's car is towed from the swamp.
In the mid-1950s, the photojournalist
recuperating from assignment-related injuries, in a cast from his hip to his foot, is wheelchair-bound in his apartment.
His mid-floor rear window looks onto a courtyard with small garden plots, surrounded on four sides by apartments in adjoining buildings.
The photojournalist is regularly visited by a nurse and his couture-clad girlfriend, a model and socialite.
The photojournalist and his girlfriend disagree about whether their relationship can survive different lifestyles.

During a heat wave, the photojournalist watches his neighbors through open windows, including a newlywed couple; a professional dancer; a songwriter with writer's block; a spinster who pantomimes dates with pretend suitors; and a traveling costume jewelry salesman, henpecked by his bedridden wife.
One night, the photojournalist hears a woman scream, followed by the sound of breaking glass.
Later that night, he observes the salesman making repeated excursions carrying his sample case.
After the photojournalist has fallen asleep, the salesman leaves his apartment along with a woman.
The next morning, the photojournalist notices that the salesman's wife seems to be gone, and the salesman is cleaning a large knife and a handsaw.
Movers haul away a large trunk.
After surveilling with binoculars and a camera's telephoto lens, the photojournalist grows suspicious of the salesman's activities.

Convinced the salesman has murdered his wife, he first tells the nurse, who becomes morbidly interested in the case, and then his girlfriend, who doubts him until they notice that the salesman's wife is no longer in bed and the mattress is rolled up.
The photojournalist calls his friend, a detective, to request that he investigate the salesman.
The skeptical detective investigates, finds nothing suspicious, and posits that the salesman sent his wife on a vacation upstate.
The photojournalist and his girlfriend are temporarily mollified by this explanation.
Later that night, however, a neighbor's dog is found dead in the courtyard; the previous day, the salesman had chased the dog away from digging his garden flowerbed.
The dog's alarmed owner cries out, drawing the attention of everyone except the salesman, who sits furtively in his dark apartment.
Now convinced his theory is true, the photojournalist looks at slides taken two weeks earlier and notices that the salesman has replanted flowers in his garden, possibly to bury a body part.
The following night, the photojournalist telephones to lure the salesman away from his apartment, enabling his girlfriend and the nurse to investigate the salesman's flowerbed.
Finding nothing, the girlfriend climbs into the salesman's open window to search his apartment.
The nurse hurries back to the photojournalist.
While the girlfriend is searching, the photojournalist and the nurse are distracted watching the spinster contemplating an overdose.
Returning unexpectedly, the salesman catches and attacks the girlfriend, causing the girlfriend to cry out.
The photojournalist calls the police to report a man assaulting a woman at the salesman's apartment.
The police arrive to intervene as the girlfriend and the salesman scuffle.
During police questioning, the girlfriend signals to the photojournalist that she is wearing the salesman's wife's wedding ring.
Seeing this, the salesman realizes the photojournalist is surveilling his apartment.
Lacking proof to accuse the salesman of murder, the girlfriend allows herself to be arrested for breaking and entering to be taken away safely.
Coincidentally, the songwriter had finished his song, playing loudly; enthralled by the tune, the spinster abandons her suicide attempt.
The photojournalist phones the detective, leaving an urgent message, while the nurse bails the girlfriend out of jail.
Locating the photojournalist's apartment, the salesman attacks him; the photojournalist's only defense in a darkened apartment is snapping his camera flash bulbs in the salesman's eyes.
While they grapple, the detective and police officers arrive, followed by the girlfriend and the nurse.
Police apprehend the salesman just as he drops the photojournalist out of his window.
The salesman confesses to his wife's murder, dumping her remains in the river, and relocating a hat box containing her head after the dog tried to dig it up.
Days later, the heat wave has broken, and life in the apartment complex has returned to normal.

The spinster is socializing with the songwriter in his studio apartment while he plays piano; the salesman's neighbors get a new puppy; the dancer's unprepossessing boyfriend returns from army deployment, and the newlyweds are more aloof.
Having broken his other leg in the fall, the photojournalist remains wheelchair-bound, now with both legs in casts.
As he naps, the girlfriend, in casual attire, surreptitiously switches from reading a book on travel exploration to a fashion magazine.
A city detective and a fellow policeman chase a crook on the roofs of several houses; the detective slips and nearly falls.
His colleague attempts to rescue the detective, but falls to his death.
Some time later, the detective has retired due to acrophobia and accompanying vertigo caused by the incident.
His ex-fiancée says that another severe emotional shock may be the only cure.
The ex-fiancée retains feelings for the detective, but he is not receptive to her intimations.
An acquaintance from college asks the detective to follow his wife, claiming that she has been behaving strangely.
The detective follows the wife to the grave of the dead woman, who died in 1857, at a mission, and to an art museum, where she gazes at a portrait of the dead woman.

A local historian explains that the dead woman committed suicide: she had been the mistress of a wealthy married man and borne his child, and the otherwise childless man kept the child and cast her aside.
The dead woman, who the husband fears is possessing the wife, was the wife's great-grandmother.
However, the wife does not know this or remember the places she has visited while ostensibly possessed.
The detective trails her to a fort and rescues her after she jumps into the bay.
The next day, the wife stops to deliver a letter of gratitude to the detective, and they spend the day together.
They travel to a forest and a point on a road, where they embrace.
The next day, the wife recounts a nightmare, and the detective identifies its setting as another mission, the dead woman's childhood home.
He drives her there, and they express their love for each other.
The wife suddenly runs into the church and up the bell tower, asking the detective not to follow her.
The detective runs after her, but is halted on the steps by his fear of heights and sees her plunge to her death.
An inquest into the wife's death declares it a suicide, though the coroner rebukes the detective for not doing more to save her.
The husband also does not fault the detective, but announces that he plans to leave the country.
The detective becomes clinically depressed and is sent to a sanatorium in an almost catatonic state.
Following his release, he frequents the places that the wife visited, often imagining that he sees her.
One day, he notices a woman on the street who, although superficially very different, reminds him of the wife.
He follows her into her apartment, where she identifies herself as a woman from another state.
A flashback reveals that the other woman was the person the detective knew as "the wife"; she had been impersonating the husband's wife in an elaborate murder scheme.
The husband took advantage of the detective's fear of heights to substitute his wife's freshly-killed body in the apparent suicide jump.
The other woman writes a note to the detective confessing her involvement in the plot, but tears it up and decides to continue the charade because she loves him.
The two begin seeing each other, but the detective remains obsessed with "the wife" and asks the other woman to change her clothes and dye her hair to resemble her.
After she complies, he notices her wearing the necklace portrayed in the dead woman's painting.
Realizing the truth, he drives the other woman back to the mission.

There, he tells her that he must re-enact the event that led to his madness, and that he now knows that "the wife" and the other woman are the same person, with the other woman having been the husband's mistress before being cast aside just as the dead woman had been.
He forces her up the bell tower and makes her admit her deceit.
The other woman confesses that the husband paid her to impersonate a "possessed" wife and begs the detective to forgive her.
He embraces the other woman at the top of the tower, but a shadowy figure—a nun investigating the noise—rises from the tower's staircase, startling her.
The other woman lunges backward off the tower to her death; the detective, bereaved once again but cured of his fear of heights, stands on the ledge in shock while the nun rings the mission bell.
In a prehistoric veld, a tribe of hominins is driven away from a water hole by a rival tribe, and the next day finds an alien monolith.
The tribe learns how to use the bones of dead animals as weapons and, after a successful first hunt, uses them to drive away the rival tribe.
Millions of years later, the chairman of a national council of astronautics travels to the base, a lunar outpost.
During a stopover at a space station, he meets foreign scientists who are concerned that the base seems to be unresponsive.
He refuses to discuss rumours of an epidemic at the base.
At the base, the chairman addresses a meeting of personnel, stressing the need for secrecy regarding their newest discovery; the rumoured epidemic is in fact a cover story.
His mission is to investigate a recently found artefact, a monolith buried four million years earlier near a lunar crater.
As the chairman and others examine and photograph the object, it emits a high-powered radio signal.

Eighteen months later, the spacecraft is bound for another planet, with mission pilots and scientists, the astronaut and his crewmate, on board, along with three other scientists in suspended animation.
Most of the ship's operations are controlled by the computer, a 9000 computer with a human-like personality.
When the computer reports the imminent failure of an antenna control device, the astronaut retrieves it in an extravehicular activity (EVA) pod, but finds nothing wrong.
The computer suggests reinstalling the device and letting it fail so the problem can be verified.
Mission control advises the astronauts that results from their twin 9000 computer indicate that the computer has made an error, but the computer blames it on human error.
Concerned about the computer's behaviour, the astronaut and his crewmate enter an EVA pod so they can talk in private without the computer overhearing.
They agree to disconnect the computer if he is proven wrong.
The computer follows their conversation by lip reading.

While the crewmate is floating away from his pod to replace the antenna unit, the computer takes control of the pod and attacks him, sending the crewmate tumbling away from the ship with a severed air line.
The astronaut takes another pod to rescue the crewmate.
While he is outside, the computer turns off the life support functions of the crewmen in suspended animation, killing them.
When the astronaut returns to the ship with the crewmate's body, the computer refuses to let him back in, stating that their plan to deactivate him jeopardises the mission.
The astronaut releases the crewmate's body and opens the ship's emergency airlock with his remote manipulators.
Lacking a helmet for his spacesuit, he positions his pod carefully so that when he jettisons the pod's door, he is propelled by the escaping air across the vacuum into the ship's airlock.
He enters the computer's processor core and begins disconnecting the computer's memory, ignoring the computer's pleas to stop.
When he is finished, a prerecorded video by the chairman plays, revealing that the mission's actual objective is to investigate the radio signal sent from the monolith to the planet.
At the planet, the astronaut finds a third, much larger monolith orbiting the planet.
He leaves the ship in an EVA pod to investigate.
He is pulled into a vortex of coloured light and observes bizarre astronomical phenomena and strange landscapes of unusual colours as he passes by.

Finally, he finds himself in a large rococo bedroom where he sees, then becomes, older versions of himself: first standing in the bedroom, middle-aged and still in his spacesuit, then dressed in leisure attire and eating dinner, and finally as an old man lying in bed.
A monolith appears at the foot of the bed, and as the astronaut reaches for it, he is transformed into a foetus enclosed in a transparent orb of light, which then floats in space above the world.
In a period of galactic civil war, rebel spies have stolen blueprints to the station, a colossal space station built by the empire that is capable of destroying entire planets.
The princess, secretly a rebel leader, has obtained the schematics, but her ship is intercepted and boarded by imperial forces under the command of the villain.
The princess is taken prisoner, but the droids escape with the plans, crash-landing on the nearby desert planet.
The villain orders his troops to pursue the droids.
The droids are captured by traders, who sell them to the moisture farmers and their nephew, the hero.
While the hero is cleaning the droid, he discovers a recording of the princess requesting help from a former ally.
The droid goes missing, and while searching for him, the hero is attacked by raiders.
He is rescued by the elderly hermit, who soon reveals himself as that former ally.
He tells the hero about his past as one of the knights, peacekeepers of the former republic, who drew mystical abilities from the field, an energy field that connects all living beings.
He explains that the knights were all but exterminated by the empire.
The hero learns that his father, also a knight, fought alongside the hermit during an earlier war until the villain, the hermit's former pupil, turned to the dark side of the field and murdered him.
The hermit gives the hero his father's sword, the signature weapon of the knights.
The droid plays the princess's full message, in which she begs the hermit to take the station plans to her home planet and give them to her father, a fellow veteran, for analysis.
The hero initially declines the hermit's offer to accompany him to the princess's home planet and learn the ways of the field.
However, he quickly changes his mind after imperial stormtroopers murder his family and destroy his home while searching for the droids.
Seeking a way off the planet, the hero and the hermit travel with the droids to the city and hire the smuggler and his partner, pilots of a starship.
On the way to the princess's home planet, the hermit begins the hero's training in the use of the field.
Meanwhile, the station, under the command of an officer, obliterates the princess's home planet with its superlaser.
It then captures the starship with a tractor beam, but the hero and his companions manage to avoid detection and infiltrate the station.
The villain, however, senses the hermit's presence, and begins searching for him.

As the hermit deactivates the tractor beam, the hero persuades the smuggler and his partner to help him rescue the princess, who is scheduled for execution after refusing to reveal the location of the rebel base.
After disabling the tractor beam, the hermit is killed by the villain in a sword duel, which allows the rest of the group to escape.
Using a tracking device placed on the starship, the empire locates the rebel base on a moon.
Analysis of the station schematics reveals a weakness in a small exhaust port leading directly to the station's reactor.
The hero joins the rebellion's fighter squadron in a desperate attack against the station, while the smuggler and his partner leave to pay off a debt to a crime lord.
In the ensuing battle, the villain leads a squadron of imperial fighters and destroys several rebel ships, while the officer prepares to destroy the moon with the station.
The smuggler and his partner unexpectedly return in the starship, knocking the villain's ship off course before he can shoot the hero down.
Guided by the voice of the hermit's spirit, the hero uses the field to aim his torpedoes into the exhaust port, causing the station to explode moments before it can fire on the rebel base.
In a triumphant ceremony, the princess awards the hero and the smuggler medals for their heroism.
In an unnamed city in 1999, a computer programmer known by an alias in hacking circles investigates the mystery of the "system", bringing him to the attention of a hacker.
She tells him that the leader can answer the programmer's questions.
At his workplace, the programmer is pursued by agents led by the villain, while the leader, able to somehow observe their movements, guides him by phone, but the programmer ultimately surrenders.
The agents interrogate the programmer about the leader, but he refuses to cooperate.
In response, they seal his mouth shut and implant a robotic tracking device in his abdomen.
The programmer awakens at home, believing the encounter was a nightmare until the hacker and her companions remove the device and take him to the leader.
The leader offers the programmer a choice: a red pill to uncover the truth about the system or a blue pill to return to his normal life.
The programmer takes the red pill and awakens in the real world, submerged in a mechanical pod and connected to invasive cables.
He sees countless humans similarly encased and tended by machines before he is ejected from the building and rescued by the leader aboard the hovercraft.
The leader explains that the year is approximately 2199.
In the 21st century, humanity lost a war against its artificially intelligent creations, leaving the planet a devastated ruin.
Humans blackened the sky to deprive the machines of solar power, but the machines retaliated by creating vast fields of artificially grown humans, harvesting their bioelectric energy.
To pacify their captives, they built the system, a simulated reality modeled on human civilization at its peak.
The remaining free humans founded an underground refuge, surviving on scarce resources.
The leader and his crew hack into the system to liberate others, exploiting its rules to gain superhuman abilities inside it.
Even so, they remain outmatched by the agents—sentient programs that protect the system—and death in the system means death in the real world.
The leader freed the programmer because he believed him to be "the one", a prophesied figure destined to free humanity.
The crew enters the system to seek guidance from the oracle, who foretold of the one.
She implies that the programmer is not the one and warns him of an imminent choice between his life and the leader's.
The crew is ambushed by agents after being betrayed by a disillusioned crew member who longs to return to the virtual comforts of the system.
Convinced of the programmer's importance, the leader sacrifices himself to confront the villain and is captured.
Meanwhile, the traitor exits the system and begins disconnecting the others, killing them.
Before he can kill the programmer and the hacker, he is killed by a wounded crew member, who extracts the survivors.
The villain interrogates the leader to obtain access codes for the refuge's mainframe, which would enable the machines to destroy the human resistance.
Determined to rescue the leader, the programmer re-enters the system with the hacker.
They free the leader, who escapes the system with the hacker, but the villain intercepts the programmer.
Realizing his potential, the programmer fights the villain as an equal and kills him.
However, the villain is resurrected in a new body and kills the programmer.
In the real world, machines attack the hovercraft.
Standing by the programmer's body, the hacker confesses her love for him and reveals that the oracle prophesied she would fall in love with the one.
In the system, the programmer revives with the ability to perceive and manipulate its code.
He effortlessly destroys the villain and escapes the system just as the hovercraft's electromagnetic pulse disables the machines.
Later, within the system, the programmer communicates with the system, vowing to show humanity a world of limitless possibilities, before flying away.
The hero and his partner are professional thieves who perform corporate espionage using experimental dream-sharing technology to infiltrate their targets' subconscious and extract information.
Their latest target is impressed with the hero's ability to layer multiple dreams within each other.

He offers to hire the hero for the ostensibly impossible job of performing "inception": implanting the heir, the son of the businessman's competitor, with the idea to dissolve his father's conglomerate.
In return, the businessman promises to clear the hero's criminal status, allowing him to return home to his children.
The hero accepts the offer and recruits a forger, a chemist, and an architecture student.
They devise a three-level dream structure in order for the heir to accept the implanted idea as his own.
The student is tasked with designing the architecture for all three levels, a task the hero himself cannot do for fear of being sabotaged by his mind's projection of his late wife.

Due to time dilation with reality, time runs slower with each descending layer, with the dreamer on each staying behind to perform a music-synchronized "kick" that simultaneously awakens dreamers on all three levels.
Once the heir's father dies, the businessman buys the airline for the heir's commercial flight to another country.
The team sedates the heir into the first level, a raining city dreamt by the chemist.

They successfully abduct the heir, but discover that he is trained to anticipate such a scenario and has subconscious defensive projections; these projections attack, severely wounding the businessman in the process.

The hero reveals that while dying in a dream usually awakens dreamers, the chemist's sedatives will instead send them into "limbo", a world of raw subconscious and extreme time dilation that is indistinguishable from reality.
The forger impersonates the heir's godfather to introduce the idea of an alternate will to dissolve the company.
The hero explains to the student that he and his wife entered limbo while experimenting with dream-sharing, experiencing fifty years in one night.
After waking up, his wife still believed she was dreaming.
Attempting to wake up, she committed suicide and framed the hero for her murder to force him to do the same.
The hero fled the country, leaving his children behind.
The chemist drives the team around the first level as they are sedated into the second level, a hotel dreamed by the partner.
The hero persuades the heir that the godfather has kidnapped him to stop the dissolution and that the hero is a defensive projection.
He leads the heir to the third level, an alpine fortress dreamt by the forger, as a ruse to enter the heir's subconscious.
In the third level, the team infiltrates the fortress with a projection of the heir's father inside, where the inception itself can be performed.

However, the chemist performs his kick too soon by driving off a bridge, forcing the partner and the forger to improvise a new set of kicks synchronized with them hitting the water by rigging an elevator and the fortress, respectively, with explosives.

The hero's wife then appears and kills the heir before he can be subjected to the inception; he and the businessman are subsequently lost in limbo, forcing the hero and the student to rescue them in time for the heir's inception and the forger's kick.

The hero reveals that during their time in limbo, his wife refused to return to reality; the hero had to convince her it was only a dream, accidentally incepting in her the belief that the real world was still a dream.
The hero makes peace with his role in his wife's death.
The student kills the wife's projection and wakes the heir up with a kick.
Revived into the third level, the heir discovers the planted idea: his dying father telling him to create something for himself.
While the hero searches for the businessman in limbo, the others ride the synced kicks back to reality.
The hero finds an aged businessman and reminds him of their agreement.
All of the dreamers awaken on the plane, and the businessman makes a phone call.
Arriving in the city, the hero passes the immigration checkpoint, and his father-in-law accompanies him to his home.
The hero uses a top that spins indefinitely in a dream to verify that he is in the real world, but joins his children before he can observe the result.

After three university parapsychology professors experience their first encounter with a ghost at the public library, the university dean dismisses the credibility of their paranormal-focused research and fires them.
The trio responds by establishing a company, a paranormal investigation and elimination service operating out of a disused firehouse.
They develop high-tech nuclear-powered equipment to capture and contain ghosts, although business is initially slow.
Following a paranormal encounter in her apartment, a cellist visits the team.
She recounts witnessing a demonic dog-like creature in her refrigerator utter a single word: a name.
The second and third professors research the name and details of the cellist's building while the first professor inspects her apartment and unsuccessfully attempts to seduce her.
The team is hired to remove a gluttonous ghost from a hotel.
Having failed to properly test their equipment, the third professor warns the group that crossing the energy streams of their proton pack weapons could cause a catastrophic explosion.
They capture the ghost and deposit it in an ecto-containment unit under the firehouse.
Supernatural activity rapidly increases across the city and the team becomes famous; they hire a fourth member to cope with the growing demand.
Suspicious of the team, an environmental agency inspector asks to evaluate their equipment, but the first professor rebuffs him.
The third professor warns that the containment unit is nearing capacity and supernatural energy is surging across the city.
The first professor meets with the cellist and informs her that the name belonged to a demigod worshipped as a servant to a shapeshifting god of destruction.
Upon returning home, the cellist is possessed by the demigod; a similar entity possesses her neighbor.
The first professor arrives and finds the possessed cellist claiming to be "the gatekeeper".
The neighbor is brought to the third professor by police officers and claims that he is "the keymaster".
The team agrees that they must keep the pair separated.
The next morning, the inspector returns with law enforcement and city workers to have the team arrested.
Against their warnings, he deactivates the containment unit, causing an explosion that releases the captured ghosts.
The possessed neighbor escapes in the confusion and makes his way to the apartment building to join the possessed cellist.

In jail, the second and third professors reveal that the leader of a god-worshipping cult in the early 20th century designed the cellist's building to function as an antenna to attract and concentrate spiritual energy to summon the god and bring about the apocalypse.
Faced with supernatural chaos across the city, the team convinces the mayor to release them.
The team travels to a hidden temple located on top of the building as the possessed cellist and neighbor open the gate between dimensions and transform into demonic dogs.
The god appears as a woman and attacks the team, then disappears when they attempt to retaliate, with its disembodied voice demanding the team "choose the form of the destructor".
The second professor inadvertently recalls a beloved corporate mascot from his childhood, and the god reappears as a gigantic marshmallow man that begins destroying the city.
Against his earlier advice, the third professor instructs the team to cross their proton energy streams at the dimensional gate.
The resulting explosion destroys the god's avatar, banishing it back to its dimension, and closes the gateway.
The team then rescues the cellist and the neighbor from the wreckage and is welcomed on the street as heroes.
